title: OpenAI chief economist says don't copy successful people's career
excerpt: Ronnie Chatterji said studying high achievers' path is "relatively bad advice" as their career journey was "very context dependent."
content_html:
OpenAI’s chief economist says copying successful people’s careers is bad advice

By Thibault Spirlet

You're currently following this author! Want to unfollow? Unsubscribe via the link in your email.

OpenAI's chief economist has some advice for workers navigating a rapidly changing job market: stop trying to replicate the careers of successful people.

Ronnie Chatterji, who is also a professor at Duke University's Fuqua School of Business, said conventional career wisdom often encourages people to study high achievers' résumés and retrace their steps.

The OpenAI exec said this is "relatively bad advice."

"People often say something like 'success leaves clues,' meaning you should follow the paths of other successful people," Chatterji said in an interview on the "Summation" podcast released on Tuesday.

But a successful person's career is rarely a useful blueprint, he said, because their public CV often leaves out periods of struggle, uncertainty, and failure. The choices that worked for them were shaped by a specific economic moment, he said.

"The path that they took whenever they took it [was] very context dependent," Chatterji said. "Very rare to find someone self-aware enough to say, you know, the way I did it won't work for you anymore. It won't work for anybody."

While Chatterji didn't name anyone, the rise of some of Silicon Valley's most prominent leaders coincided with era-defining technological shifts.

Mark Zuckerberg built Facebook as growing internet access helped social networking go mainstream, Jeff Bezos founded Amazon as e-commerce took off, and Sam Altman has led OpenAI through the generative AI boom, enabled in part by increasingly powerful chips.

"The economic environment matters; it determines when the best time to found a company is, for example," Chatterji said. "Those things depend on the dynamism of the economy."

The skills that endure in the age of AI

The advice lands as AI forces workers to reconsider which jobs and skills will remain valuable.

Chatterji said coding, maths, formal reasoning, and an understanding of how AI works will remain important. He also said judgment, flexibility, resilience, and the ability to identify worthwhile problems will become more valuable as AI takes on more tasks.

That puts him in line with a growing body of advice from tech leaders and AI workers over the past year.

Phil Chen, a former OpenAI researcher who also worked at Google DeepMind and Scale AI, said this month that "problem selection and resource allocation" will be the most important skills as AI handles more complex, well-defined work.

Former Google executive Mo Gawdat has urged job seekers to learn AI tools while leaning into human-centric work, while OpenAI president Greg Brockman has described "taste" — knowing what to keep — as a new core skill. Prashanthi Padmanabhan, LinkedIn's vice president of engineering for Talent Solutions, has also highlighted "critical thinking, problem solving, collaboration, and teamwork" as skills workers need alongside technical ability.

Rather than modeling their lives on a founder, executive, investor, or other career hero, workers should focus on the problems they want to solve and try to position themselves where those problems are being tackled, Chatterji said.

"We should use our heroes, our career heroes, our occupational heroes for inspiration but not step-by-step advice," Chatterji said.

"Success leaves clues, but it's not in the step-by-step," Chatterji added. "It's often in the habits."

OpenAI 首席经济学家表示，复制成功人士的职业生涯是个糟糕的建议

作者：Thibault Spirlet 您目前正在关注该作者！ 想要取消关注吗？ 通过电子邮件中的链接取消订阅。

OpenAI 的首席经济学家对应对快速变化的就业市场的工人提出了一些建议：不要试图复制成功人士的职业生涯。

杜克大学福卡商学院教授罗尼·查特吉 (Ronnie Chatterji) 表示，传统的职业智慧经常鼓励人们研究高成就者的简历并回顾他们的脚步。

OpenAI 高管表示，这是“相对糟糕的建议”。

“人们经常说‘成功留下线索’之类的话，意思是你应该追随其他成功人士的道路，”查特吉在周二发布的“Summation”播客上接受采访时说道。

但他说，成功人士的职业生涯很少是有用的蓝图，因为他们的公开简历常常会遗漏挣扎、不确定和失败的时期。 他说，对他们有用的选择是由特定的经济时刻决定的。

“他们无论何时选择的道路都非常依赖于环境，”查特吉说。 “很少有人有足够的自我意识来说，你知道，我所做的方式不再适合你了。 这对任何人都不起作用。”

虽然查特吉没有透露任何人的名字，但硅谷一些最著名领导人的崛起恰逢定义时代的技术变革。

随着互联网接入的不断增长，社交网络成为主流，马克·扎克伯格 (Mark Zuckerberg) 创建了 Facebook；随着电子商务的腾飞，杰夫·贝索斯 (Jeff Bezos) 创建了亚马逊；萨姆·奥尔特曼 (Sam Altman) 带领 OpenAI 经历了生成式 AI 热潮，这在一定程度上得益于日益强大的芯片。

“经济环境很重要；例如，它决定了成立公司的最佳时机，”查特吉说。 “这些事情取决于经济的活力。”

人工智能时代经久不衰的技能

随着人工智能迫使工人重新考虑哪些工作和技能仍然有价值，这一建议得到了落实。

查特吉表示，编码、数学、形式推理以及对人工智能工作原理的理解仍然很重要。 他还表示，随着人工智能承担更多任务，判断力、灵活性、弹性和识别有价值问题的能力将变得更有价值。

这使他与过去一年中技术领导者和人工智能工作者越来越多的建议保持一致。

曾在 Google DeepMind 和 Scale AI 工作过的前 OpenAI 研究员 Phil Chen 本月表示，随着人工智能处理更复杂、定义明确的工作，“问题选择和资源分配”将是最重要的技能。

谷歌前高管 Mo Gawdat 敦促求职者学习人工智能工具，同时倾向于以人为本的工作，而 OpenAI 总裁格雷格·布罗克曼 (Greg Brockman) 将“品味”——知道该保留什么——描述为一项新的核心技能。 LinkedIn 人才解决方案工程副总裁 Prashanthi Padmanabhan 也强调了“批判性思维、解决问题、协作和团队合作”是员工除了技术能力之外还需要的技能。

查特吉说，员工不应以创始人、高管、投资者或其他职业英雄为榜样，而应专注于他们想要解决的问题，并努力将自己定位在正在解决这些问题的地方。

查特吉说：“我们应该利用我们的英雄、我们的职业英雄、我们的职业英雄来获取灵感，而不是一步一步的建议。”

“成功会留下线索，但并不在于一步一步，”查特吉补充道。 “这通常是在习惯中。”
